body:
Rafael Mendes: planning thread for the overload protection game day. goal: validate breakers + deterministic shedding end-to-end (gateway → routing → runtime) AND make sure oncall playbook is sane.

Rafael Mendes: proposing next Thu 10:00–12:00 PT. Connor can you confirm if that works for release window + who needs to be in the Zoom?

Connor O'Brien: Thu 10–12 PT is good. no major releases in that slot. I’ll set up Zoom + calendar and add eng-sre + platform + runtime. We’ll do a quick “freeze” on config changes during the exercise except for the planned toggles.

Christine Wong: +1. we should lock the breaker config in staging before the game day so we’re not debugging drift.

Tomáš Novák: can we align on scenarios + pass/fail criteria here, then I’ll copy into the runbook + game day doc.

Aisha Bello: pls also call out what dashboards/alerts we expect to light up (and what should NOT page). last drill we got noisy 5xx alerts that weren’t actionable.

Rafael Mendes: yup. I’ll start a draft list of scenarios. add/modify as needed:
1) step-function traffic spike (2x→6x in 60s) on a single popular hosted model in us-east
2) long-prompt spike (prefill heavy) causing queue growth + KV/cache pressure
3) regional brownout simulation: reduce available GPUs / capacity signals show saturation
4) client retry storm simulation: high concurrency + no jitter to validate we return Retry-After + avoid cascading retries
5) breaker flapping regression check: oscillating load around threshold to ensure hysteresis works
6) control-plane stress: routing eval API latency under load (ensure it stays responsive)

Rafael Mendes: expected behavior across all: shed early when possible, error semantics stable (429/503 + Redwood error codes), no tail-latency collapse for admitted traffic, breaker state transitions visible and rate-limited.

Mina Haddad: for (1) and (3) we need to validate routing fallback interaction. i.e. if primary (model,region,tier) breaker opens, can we safely fall back to compatible region/model variant when policy allows. also confirm we don’t end up in a fallback loop.

Elena Popov: +1. also need a scenario where fallback is intentionally disabled (tier mismatch / customer policy) so we verify the “hard fail” behavior is still clean.

Amara Diallo: for gateway side: I want to explicitly test shed at edge vs shed after routing eval. We should see `x-redwood-overload: edge_admission` vs `routing_breaker` (whatever header we settled on) so support can explain.

Allison Grant: note on telemetry: for the drill we should confirm we’re emitting the standard tags without blowing cardinality. route/model/region/tier ok; no customer_id label in metrics. if someone needs per-tenant, use traces/logs sampling.

Sergio Costa: I can put a mini “game day dashboard” playlist together: shed_rate, breaker_state, queue_depth, routing_eval_latency, gateway_429/503 split, p95/p99 per route. Also add a panel for Retry-After distribution.

Aisha Bello: can we add an explicit pass/fail line: “load shedding errors do NOT burn the internal error-budget and do NOT trigger Sev paging unless thresholds exceeded”? want to ensure oncall doesn’t auto-declare an incident when breakers do their job.

Rafael Mendes: yes. we’ll define what’s “expected overload-protected” vs “unexpected internal 5xx”.

Tomáš Novák: can someone define the exact load generator patterns for scenarios (1) + (2)? like prompts, target TPS, streaming vs non-streaming mix.

Peter Holtz: I can own the loadgen setup. propose:
- Scenario 1: chat completions, 70% streaming, avg 350 output tokens, step from 300 rps → 1200 rps in 60s, hold 10 min.
- Scenario 2: 30% streaming, long prompts (8k–16k tokens), output 200 tokens, ramp 100 rps → 400 rps, hold 10 min.
We’ll run in staging us-east first, then optionally canary-prod with guardrails.

Christine Wong: for breaker thresholds, we should test both “soft open” and “hard open” paths.
- soft open: shed new requests but allow in-flight to drain
- hard open: shed immediately at gateway for that key to protect routing/runtime
Expected: hard open only when routing signals indicate severe saturation OR routing eval itself is degraded.

Amara Diallo: I’ll add a switch in the gateway feature flag panel for the drill so we can flip between “edge shed enabled” and “edge shed disabled” (to prove downstream shed still works). I’ll document the exact flag names.

Ravi Menon: for routing capacity signals, let’s simulate lag too. i.e. stale GPU utilization signal for ~30s. expected: breaker shouldn’t oscillate wildly; should rely on queue depth / request timeout signals as backup.

Allison Grant: careful with “simulate lag” – easiest is to pin the signal publisher to a slower refresh in staging. But please don’t do per-request labels to debug; use trace exemplars.

Sergio Costa: I’ll add a debug annotation stream on the dashboard for breaker transitions (closed→open→half-open) so we can correlate with traffic phases.

Rafael Mendes: owners per scenario (proposed):
- Scenario 1 (step spike): Peter (loadgen), Christine (breaker config), Amara (gateway), Sergio (dashboard), Mina/Ravi (routing fallback)
- Scenario 2 (long prompt/KV pressure): Peter (loadgen), Mina/Ravi (routing), Christine (breaker thresholds), Allison (metrics sanity), runtime observers TBD (not in this channel)
- Scenario 3 (regional brownout/capacity reduction): Ravi/Elena (capacity signals + routing), Amara (edge mapping), Sergio (dashboard)
- Scenario 4 (retry storm): Amara (gateway headers + error mapping), Aisha (SLO / paging expectations), Peter (load profile)
- Scenario 5 (flapping): Christine (hysteresis/cooldown), Sergio (visualize transitions), Tomáš (note learnings + follow-ups)
- Scenario 6 (control-plane stress): Mina (routing service SLO), Rafael (incident commander role), Aisha (alert verification)

Tomáš Novák: I can be scribe + “what would we do in prod” reviewer. also will capture: what manual mitigations we used + how long to recover.

Aisha Bello: for Scenario 4, expected client guidance:
- return 429 when we’re shedding at edge due to admission control (retryable)
- return 503 when downstream breaker open / no capacity and policy says no fallback (retryable)
- always include Retry-After (seconds) + Redwood error code
- do NOT return ambiguous 500/502 for overload
We should verify the SDK wrappers surface Retry-After.

Amara Diallo: for gateway behavior under load: verify we don’t spend CPU building giant error bodies. keep it small JSON and early return.

Allison Grant: and verify we’re sampling traces on shed paths (like 1%) so we have examples, but not flooding.

Christine Wong: half-open behavior test: after cooldown, allow small probe rate. expected: if probes succeed, close; if not, reopen with exponential backoff. we should define probe budget (e.g., 1% or fixed N rps).

Rafael Mendes: +1. Christine can you drop the planned half-open probe numbers we’re using in staging? (just so everyone knows what to expect)

Christine Wong: current staging defaults:
- open_cooldown: 60s
- half_open_probe_rps: 5 rps per (model,region,tier)
- half_open_window: 30s
- close_if_success_rate >= 0.98 AND p99 < 2.5s
- reopen_if_success_rate < 0.95 OR p99 > 4.0s
We can tune after drill.

Sergio Costa: I’ll ensure the dashboard has panels for probe rate + probe success.

Connor O'Brien: logistics: we should explicitly decide if we’re running in staging only. if we touch prod at all, we need a change ticket + comms in #eng-releases and a rollback plan.

Rafael Mendes: preference: do full drill in staging, then optional 15-min limited prod canary (single route, single region) IF staging results look clean and Connor approves. No surprises.

Peter Holtz: I’ll prep both environments but default to staging. For the optional prod canary I’ll cap at low rps and use a dedicated test key.

Tomáš Novák: can we add one more “manual override” scenario? simulate “breaker too aggressive” and we flip the admin toggle to disable new breaker logic in one region. expected: immediate reduction in 429s but watch latency/queue depth to ensure we don’t cause a cascade.

Rafael Mendes: good call. add Scenario 7: “emergency toggle/rollback”. Owner: Christine + Connor (change control), Amara (gateway flag), Sergio (watch metrics), Rafael as IC.

incident-bot: Reminder: if you run a prod canary, use /incident annotate with start/end times and include region/model/flag state in the annotation.

Aisha Bello: pass/fail criteria draft:
PASS if:
- p99 for admitted traffic stays within +20% of baseline during spike
- shed rate increases but internal 5xx does not spike
- breaker opens within 30s of sustained saturation and remains stable (no >3 transitions/min)
- Retry-After present on >99% of 429/503
- routing eval p99 < 200ms under load
- alerts: only “overload active” informational alerts fire; no Sev paging unless internal errors occur
FAIL if:
- routing/control plane becomes unavailable
- we see retry storm amplification (RPS keeps increasing after shed)
- error semantics inconsistent (500/502 bursts) or missing headers

Rafael Mendes: looks good. Tomáš can you paste that into the game day doc + add a section for “notes / follow-ups” so we track action items?

Tomáš Novák: yup, will do today.

Mina Haddad: one more expected behavior: when fallback is allowed, ensure we set an explicit response header indicating fallback occurred (or at least log it) so support can explain why output quality/latency changed.

Elena Popov: +1. also ensure fallback doesn’t violate tier boundaries (e.g., don’t route free tier onto protected capacity).

Amara Diallo: I’ll verify we have the right header for fallback and that it’s not leaking internal details. maybe `x-redwood-fallback: region` or similar.

Allison Grant: please keep headers bounded / not including internal IDs.

Rafael Mendes: action items:
- Connor: calendar + Zoom + change freeze note
- Peter: loadgen scripts + environment config
- Sergio: dashboard playlist + annotations
- Christine: breaker config snapshot + half-open probe metrics in dashboard
- Tomáš: update game day doc + pass/fail
- Amara: gateway flags + header validation checklist
- Aisha: alert expectations + confirm paging rules with oncall

Rafael Mendes: anything else before I close this thread?

Sergio Costa: small ask: during the drill, please call out exact flag flips in-channel so I can add annotations. otherwise we’ll lose correlation.

Christine Wong: +1. we should have a single “control” channel during the drill (maybe #eng-sre-warroom) so updates are centralized.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll create #warroom-overload-gameday for the 2h window + post checklist + link to dashboard.

Rafael Mendes: perfect. thanks all.
